Yes, with limitations: the Source Pack supports a source-grounded review of Caesars' operating history, Q2 2026 results, reported debt and liquidity, selected note terms, the pending merger and a few public bond observations, but it is not a complete underwriting pack. Of the 21 prepared files, 18 were delivered whole and 3 as page maps; none is Blocked. Readiness is Restricted. [C8, C9, C10]

The period boundary is the first limit. The FY2025 10-K and the 30 June 2026 10-Q give audited annual and unaudited interim figures; there is no Q3 filing or later operating update, so June figures must not be read as October figures. [C8, C9, C10]

The legal and debt limits come next. The base 2032 secured indenture, the Incremental Assumption Agreement No. 3 and the fund prospectus are page-mapped. The supplemental indentures and the fourth and fifth credit amendments are present, but the complete current CEI Credit Agreement and the collateral and intercreditor package are not, so covenant capacity and security cannot be established from this pack. The 10-K reports US$11.9bn of indebtedness and about US$1.4bn of 2026 VICI and GLPI rent; the 10-Q reports debt-table figures and long-term financing obligations. Face principal, carrying value and financing obligations are distinct bases. [C11, C12, C13]

Market evidence is thin. The four FINRA pages show 1 October last trades, not bids or evaluated prices, and the fund schedule values a Caesars secured-note position at 30 June. The merger agreement and 8-K give the US$31.00 cash price, but the debt commitment papers, schedules and the amount of new debt are not in the pack. [C14, C15, C16, C17, C18]

CP-1.analysis_md:
The canonical record answers the reader question with audited annual and unaudited interim figures: FY2025 net revenues were 11,486 and Adjusted EBITDA 3,624, H1 2026 revenue rose 2.8% to 5,863 while Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.7% to 1,807, and in Q2 revenue grew 3.0% while Adjusted EBITDA fell 3.7% to 920 [C140, C133, C141, C142]. LTM Adjusted EBITDA to 30 June 2026 is 3592 and face debt 11807, so total leverage is 3.29x (calc: total leverage on face debt = 11807 / 3592 = 3.29x) [C132]. USD millions throughout; confidence is Restricted.

RBOT counts debt at face principal because the facility register is built from the debt note: 11,905 at 31 December 2025 and 11,807 at 30 June 2026. Balance-sheet carrying debt is lower, at 11,699 on the same date after discounts and deferred finance charges, so the two measures are not interchangeable [C130, C131, C132]. The GLPI and VICI financing obligations of 13,157 sit outside debt, and the filing estimates about 1.4 billion of 2026 lease payments to them, so debt-only leverage understates fixed claims [C143].

Reported EBITDA is operating income plus D&A, and Adjusted EBITDA adds back impairment, transaction costs and stock-based compensation. That bridge closes exactly in every column, for example 3,275 plus 349 of add-backs gives 3,624 for FY2025 [C133]. Segment history shows the mix shift: Las Vegas revenue fell to 4,049 in FY2025 while Regional held at 5,756 and Digital grew to 1,408; in Q2 2026 Regional rose to 1,570 and Las Vegas fell to 1,017 [C144, C145]. For creditors this is uneven cash generation, and one segment's strength should not be read as consolidated deleveraging without cash-flow confirmation.

Operating cash flow was 1,302 in FY2025 and 675 in H1 2026, against property and equipment purchases of 805 and 335 [C136, C146, C137, C147]. Cash interest paid for debt was 813 in FY2025 and 368 in H1 2026, with a further 1,349 and 686 of lease cash on the financing obligations [C134, C135]. Quarterly cash flows are not disclosed for Q2, so quarterly cash conversion is not established. Customer deposits and deferred revenue of 545 at 30 June are a funding float, not debt [C148].

What would change this view: sustained segment EBITDA, disclosed covenant headroom and debt reduction would strengthen it; lower H1 EBITDA, large lease commitments and the absence of any post-June reporting hold it back. The Alberta launch on 13 July 2026 is a subsequent event and is excluded from Q2 figures [C149]. Confidence in this module: Medium-Low.

CP-1A.analysis_md:
Four facts matter most to a creditor. Caesars is a large, lease-heavy and gaming-led operator whose Las Vegas segment is weakening while Regional grows partly through the Windsor consolidation; it has agreed to a US$31.00 cash take-private by Fertitta Gaming Holdco that is conditional and still pending, and the size of the new debt is not stated in the sources. [C78, C79, C52, C67, C80]

Operating model. FY2025 net revenue was US$11.486bn, led by casino at US$6.617bn, with hotel US$1.945bn, food and beverage US$1.714bn and other US$1.210bn. H1 2026 revenue rose to US$5.863bn from US$5.701bn while Adjusted EBITDA fell to US$1.807bn from US$1.839bn. For creditors, hold, visitation, labour, taxes and rent decide how much revenue reaches cash. [C81, C82, C83, C84, C85, C86]

Transaction and ownership. The signed agreement keeps Caesars as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent after the merger. The Carano family, with about 5%, rolls part of its stake. A US$200m company termination fee and a US$450m reverse fee apply in defined cases, and Parent's financing is not a closing condition. Funding terms, schedules and post-close capitalisation are not in the pack, so no closing probability is inferred and pro forma leverage rests on the three synthetic tranches of this test run. [C52, C87, C88]

Governance view: Medium and incomplete. Reporting is audited and regular, and no repurchases were made in H1 2026, but acquisitions, a US$229m 2025 buyback and a small related-party lease are monitored items. [C63, C64, C89, C90]

Ratings: the pack shows issue ratings only, from FINRA (Moody's B1 and S&P BB- on the secured 2032s, Caa1 and B- on the unsecured 2032s). The corporate family rating B1 negative and S&P BB- on CreditWatch negative in the register are synthetic test values, marked as such, because no agency report was supplied. The downside path is a merger delay or weaker Las Vegas trading consuming cash while debt service and rent persist; the disclosed US$10m of merger costs is the first visible cost. [C80, C91]

CP-1D.analysis_md:
Only part of Adjusted EBITDA is supported by evidence: three exclusions are open and none can be fully accepted. Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's own measure, and its reconciliation excludes impairment (US$182m in FY2025), a grouped transaction-and-other line (US$72m) and stock-based compensation (US$95m). CAOS found impairment and stock compensation recurring in every annual period and rejected them as exceptional; the transaction line recurs but mixes unlike items, so it stays unresolved. [C1, C2, C4, C15]

This module records all three as Challenged and keeps them in house EBITDA so the Model ties to the issuer's US$3,592m LTM figure. If the impairment and stock-compensation exclusions were rejected, LTM EBITDA would be US$3,318m and debt-to-EBITDA 3.56x against 3.29x (US$3,500m and 3.37x for stock compensation alone). [C16, C3, C5]

Cash conversion is weak. FY2025 cash from operations was US$1,302m on US$3,624m of Adjusted EBITDA (35.9%), H1 2026 US$675m on US$1,807m (37.4%), and the LTM figure 36.1%. Capex, H1 cash interest of US$368m and rent interest still come out of that cash. [C17, C18, C19]

Debt-like items. The balance sheet carries US$13,157m of long-term financing obligations on the VICI and GLPI leases outside reported debt. Adding them once to face debt of US$11,807m gives US$24,964m, or 6.95x LTM Adjusted EBITDA against 3.29x on debt alone (the CAOS carrying-value basis gives at least 6.92x). The FY2025 operating-lease liability (US$742m) and finance-lease liability (US$147m) are shown but not added: June balances are not disclosed and the finance-lease overlap is unreconciled. [C20, C21, C22, C23, C24]

Counterweight and trigger: the reconciliation is transparent, impairment is non-cash and cash flow is positive. That would carry more weight if a component bridge showed the transaction costs were settled one-offs and conversion improved after capex and rent. Watch repeated impairment, stock compensation, conversion below 36% and rising revolver use. The H1 2026 tax line shows a dash in the 10-Q where CP-1 carries a zero; it is flagged for CP-1 to reconcile. [C25]

CP-4.analysis_md:
The documented package protects creditors with guarantees, collateral and sacred-right thresholds, but it is mainly an incurrence-covenant structure: the notes carry no maintenance test, and the facility tests apply only to the revolver and Term Loan A [C66][C68]. The supported risk is potential incremental leverage and value leakage through contractual baskets, not a demonstrated breach or a completed priming event. The real CAOS CP-4 put overall aggressiveness at 4 of 5, which is a protection score of 2 of 5 here, at confidence 57 of 100 and QA Restricted.

On RBOT's basis (company LTM Adjusted EBITDA and face debt) every tested covenant has room. Net leverage is 3.02x against a maximum of 6.50x, headroom 3.48x (calc: Total Leverage Ratio (revolver and Term Loan A) headroom = 6.5 - 3.02 = 3.48x); cash interest cover is 4.63x against a minimum of 2.00x, headroom 2.63x. The covenant EBITDA and net debt definitions are not reconciled to the company's Adjusted EBITDA (G34), so these are indicative, and compliance at 30 June is reported but headroom is not [C68].

With the three synthetic merger tranches layered on [C44], net leverage rises to 4.41x (headroom 2.09x), senior secured leverage to 3.75x against the 4.50x pari test (headroom 0.75x) and cash interest cover falls to 3.10x (headroom 1.10x). All stay in Headroom, so the new debt is covenant-feasible while using most of the pari secured capacity.

Capacity is the central creditor risk. The pari secured test allows about 6,696 of further first-lien debt and the junior test about 7,594 [C27][C32][C33][C36][C37][C38][C39][C40][C41][C42]; these are alternatives, not additive. The restricted-payment and investment baskets were not extracted (G32), so the register fills them with synthetic sizes and usage: a builder basket of 1,450 with 300 used, a general restricted-payment basket of 500 and a general investment basket of 750. The free-and-clear and general debt baskets stay Not computable because usage is not disclosed (G33).

What would change this view: the full current credit agreement, the intercreditor agreement and a compliance certificate with basket usage would let the headroom be recomputed on covenant definitions and the leakage capacity be sized. A Term Loan B-1 amendment, a drop-down into an unrestricted subsidiary or a new pari financing would deteriorate the view. Confidence in this module: Low.

The market is pricing Caesars as a stressed-looking high-yield credit, but the signal has low diagnostic precision and no implied default probability should be quoted from it. The October 1 FINRA last trades put the secured 2032s at 93.28 to yield 8.06352% and the unsecured 2032s at 84.94 to yield 9.318398% [C1][C2][C7][C8]. The real CAOS run reached the same conclusion at confidence 44 of 100 [C42, C43, C44, C45, C46].

MGM's 6.125% 2029s (6.722997%) and PENN's 4.125% 2029s (6.644415%) [C13][C18] mature three years earlier and are context only.

To make the observations comparable the fixture converts each yield to a spread over a synthetic 6-year Treasury of 4.10% [C6]: 396 bps for the secured and 522 bps for the unsecured notes. A credit-triangle hazard with a single synthetic recovery of 40% [C26] gives annual implied hazards of 6.6% and 8.7%; these rank the securities by spread and are not forecasts. The term loans carry synthetic dealer quotes [C22] and are shown on a 3-year discount margin basis.

One observation is stale and is kept for what it shows: the fund's 30 June valuation of the secured 2032s was 97.62 [C27], 4.34 points above the October last trade. It is an evaluated price at another date, flagged Stale, and carries no spread.
